title: Cross-functional release dry-run template & risk playbook (working draft)
summary: Working draft of a cross-functional dry-run template and risk playbook intended to encode a repeatable rehearsal for canary and A/B releases. Focus: reduce surprise during live activations by validating telemetry, comms, gates, and rollback orchestration in a coordinated dry run with synthetic and sampled traffic.
objectives: Validate end-to-end activation choreography across eng, SRE, product and CS
Confirm observability and alerting thresholds for canaries and sliced A/B cohorts
Exercise rollback and fallback automation paths under simulated faults
Ensure communication cadence and stakeholder handoff is crisp and timeboxed
Surface gaps in signal coverage (latency, error modes, quality regressions) before production exposure
preconditions: Build artifacts for both control and variant model/service are published to prod stage
Telemetry plumbing (metrics, distributed traces, logs) identified and testable endpoints ready
Synthetic traffic harness deployed to mimic representative user journeys
Oncall roster and primary/secondary stewards assigned and paged into the dry run
Rollback playbooks loaded into the console and validated via dry-run-only toggles
dryrun-checklist: Kickoff meeting (10m): review goals, blast radius, timeline, owners
Smoke activation: flip feature-flag for 0% traffic and validate config propagation
Synthetic traffic sweep: generate low-volume requests to exercise happy path
Telemetry check: confirm metrics appear in dashboards and traces link with request ids
Canary slice: enable 1% traffic to variant and validate latency/throughput baselines
A/B routing: verify experiment assignment logic and cohort integrity
Failure injection 1: throttle upstream DB for 30s while observing degradation behavior
Failure injection 2: kill a single model-serving pod and confirm fallback model selection
Rollback drill: trigger an automated rollback and validate rollback indicators and comms
Post-dryrun retro: capture missing signals, unclear owner handoffs, and config bugs
observability-assertions: Per-route p50/p95/p99 latency is emitted with tags: model, region, slice
Token-level cost per request aggregated by model variant is available in console
Quality signal: nlu-confidence and rerank-score distributions reported for both cohorts
Error budgets and SLO dashboards reflect canary impact within minutes
Synthetic traffic trace ids surface across logs -> traces -> metrics to validate full linkage
gating-criteria: No increase > 2x in p95 latency for canary vs control over a 15-minute window
Error rate delta < 0.1% absolute compared to control during the canary window
Quality regression: automated eval on 1000 synthetic prompts shows no >3% drop in top-1 accuracy
No new high-severity security or privacy alerts flagged by policy scanners
Cost spike: per-token cost for variant not exceeding budget threshold for sustained 30m window
rollback-triggers: Sustained p95 latency increase >2x for 15m despite autoscaling attempts
Error rate crossing SLO breach for two consecutive 5-minute buckets
Automated eval detects semantic hallucination patterns above configured threshold
Critical downstream dependency failures (DB, auth) causing request drop >5% of traffic
Manual operator judgement: product or SRE signals user-impacting behavioral regressions
roles-and-responsibilities: Release Owner: coordinates run, declares go/no-go and calls rollback
SRE Steward: owns infra-side rollback, autoscaling overrides, and incident timeline
Product Lead: monitors quality metrics and customer-facing signal; signs off on canary progression
Metrics Owner: ensures dashboards and alerts are wired and interprets early drift
Solutions/CS Rep: watches high-value customer cohorts and prepares comms if exposure is expanded
Developer on-call: ready to apply hotfix and pair with SRE for rollout reversion
Communications Lead: posts staged updates to stakeholder channels and updates status page
comms-templates: Pre-dryrun announcement (slack): "Dry-run starting at T+0. Owners: Sofia (release), Marcus (SRE), Priya (product). Sim traffic and two failure injections planned. Expected duration 45m. Please stand by on #release-coordination."
Rollback notice (email/incident): "ACTION: rolling back variant X to control at 15:23Z due to elevated p95 latency. Users impacted: internal sim only. Follow postmortem template RL-348."
Incident pager blurb: "Alert: canary p95 > threshold. If you are Release Owner, acknowledge and execute rollback path A. Oncall SRE to verify circuit breaker."
Post-dryrun summary (doc): short bullets of what we practiced, gaps found, owners for fixes, and date for follow-up rehearse"
simulation-scenarios: Baseline: normal distributed traffic for 30 minutes to establish baselines
Burst load: sustained 4x traffic for 5 minutes to test autoscaler and latency tail behavior
Cold-start storm: mass of new sessions to exercise model cold KV cache warming
Dependency degradation: partial DB unavailability to observe graceful failure and fallback latency
Quality perturbation: synthetic prompts designed to trigger edge-case hallucinations for variant
cost-and-latency-budget: Set explicit per-release budgets: e.g., incremental per-token cost cap of $0.003 per active concurrent request and p95 latency budget of 450ms across regions. If either budget is exceeded for 30m, pause rollout and triage.
unresolved-questions: Do we need a dedicated dry-run staging account to isolate quota/billing noise?
Should rollback be automatic on first critical signal or gated by Release Owner acknowledgement?
Which customer cohorts require manual opt-in for A/B exposure during early canaries?
How do we mark synthetic traffic in telemetry to prevent polluting long-term metrics?
next-steps: Schedule 1 full dry-run with cross-functional attendees in the next sprint (owner: Sofia)
Add synthetic-traffic tag to metrics pipeline and instrument trace linking (owner: Marcus)
Formalize autoscaling override play into SRE runbooks and test in dry-run (owner: Tomás)
